title: Standout stars
caption: The globular cluster NGC 3201, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 3201 · constellation Vela · about 16000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #84 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble image looks into NGC 3201, a glistening, ancient globular cluster of hundreds of thousands of stars held together by gravity. James Dunlop found it in 1826 and described it as 'pretty large, pretty bright', becoming 'rather irregular' toward its center.

Globular clusters surround all large galaxies, yet how they formed and what part they played in building galaxies is still unclear. NGC 3201 recently added a twist. Astronomers found a black hole at its heart, betrayed by a star being flung quickly around a massive, invisible partner.

The cluster also stands out among the Milky Way's more than 150 globulars. It moves extremely fast relative to the Sun, and its orbit around the galactic center is retrograde, running against the usual direction. That behavior hints that it may have come from outside our galaxy and been captured. Its stars, however, are chemically very like those of other globulars in the Milky Way, suggesting they formed at a similar place and time.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.51 x 2.59 arcminutes) and distance (16000 light years), the frame spans roughly 12 × 12 light-years. Its light set out about 16,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This view combines Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 in ultraviolet and near-ultraviolet light with its Advanced Camera for Surveys in visible and near-infrared light. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The ultraviolet and near-infrared light are invisible to the eye, and the black hole at the cluster's heart cannot be seen at all. It was found only through a star's motion.

explore: The cluster lies about 16,000 light-years away in the constellation Vela. Whether it was adopted by the Milky Way or simply evolved differently from the clusters it grew up with remains an open question.
alt: A dense, glistening gathering of stars in the globular cluster NGC 3201.
